Subject: [BrightArc] Intermittent empty responses from /v1/generate

Hi team,

We started seeing intermittent empty responses from the /v1/generate endpoint this morning (samples attached).  Two different users hit the same prompt around 08:53 and got back an empty payload (200 OK, body length ~0).  No obvious client-side exceptions.

Attached: session_log_0628.txt (truncated), screenshot_error_1.png

Can you confirm whether this is a service issue or if we should look more closely at our client? These queries are important for our recommendations flow.

Thanks,

From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: [BrightArc] Intermittent empty responses from /v1/generate

On Mon, Jun 28, 2027 at 09:28 AM olga.petrov@redwood.ai wrote:
> Rishi / infra: can you pick this up?

I've run reproduction attempts against the exact model (stable-llama-30B) and the payloads included in the session_log_0628.txt. Summary of findings:

1) Reproduction: 30 attempts from our EU/us infra during a 3-hour window overlapping BrightArc timestamps — no empty-response returns observed. All responses contained tokens and matched expected length distributions.

2) Serving logs: we cross-referenced request-ids (where present) against runtime logs. The requests in the provided log show normal kernel execution with no OOM, no SIGTERM, and no truncation warnings. KV-cache usage looked normal.

3) Network / proxy: HTTP front-door shows 200 with Content-Length > 0 for all recorded responses. There is one instance where a keep-alive connection reset occurred between LB and client around 08:54:11; in that case the client disconnected before the full body arrived. That could present to a client as an "empty" payload depending on the client library behavior.

4) Quantization/kernel: no evidence of kernel failure or quantization-induced short-circuits.

Action items/next steps I recommend:
- Ask BrightArc to include request-id/header and raw response length when they observe the empty output. If the client disconnects mid-stream the server may have emitted tokens that never reached the client.
- If they can share the raw tcpdump or client-side logs showing the connect/reset sequence, we can correlate at the load-balancer.

Given current evidence I can't attribute an internal runtime failure. I'll keep monitoring for correlated anomalies (spike of keep-alive resets) but for now this looks like a client-side network/delivery issue in at least one observed case.

Rishi
Senior Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: olga.petrov@redwood.ai <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Joshi <samir@brightarc.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai, vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 30 Jun 2027 16:25:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: [BrightArc] Intermittent empty responses from /v1/generate — outcome and recommended next steps

Hi Samir — quick follow-up with what our infra team found after triage:

Summary of investigation:
- We reproduced against the same model and payloads and did not see empty bodies returned from Redwood's runtime.
- Runtime logs and serving telemetry for the sample timestamps show successful kernel execution and response emission.
- We did observe one LB -> client connection reset that occurred at roughly the same time as one of your samples; if the BrightArc client closed the connection early it would appear as an empty body on your side.

Recommended next steps for BrightArc (minimal):
1) When you see an empty response, reply to this thread with the exact request-id (if present), timestamp, and client log snippet showing the connect/reset. That will let us correlate LB traces to a single request.
2) Consider a short client-side retry (idempotent) for these RPCs — we can suggest a safe retry policy if you'd like.
3) If you prefer we can provision a short capture window on the LB to gather PCAPs during the next 24–72 hours — let me know and we'll coordinate with your on-call to time it.

Outcome: no server-side bug found. We are closing the internal incident as "no internal evidence" but will reopen immediately if you can provide a request-id or client-side trace that reproduces the condition.

Thanks for raising this, and please keep sending any samples — we'll watch the LB metrics and backstop with a capture window if you want.

Best,
Olga Petrov
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
